transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is defending himself amid a wave of criticism.
He held a rare press conference, his first in six months,
in the face of an impeachment effort in the House
of Representatives during the lame duck session of Congress.
NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports.
>> The press conference comes a day after Republican Congressman Thomas Massie
introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth
over his handling of the war in Iran and other military operations.
Hegseth began by addressing the move to impeach him,
calling it a, quote, "political spectacle."
>> It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it.
>> Congressman Massie has accused Hegseth of violating laws
against harming civilians and violating the Constitution and federal law
by ignoring the will of Congress to carry out the war in Iran,
among other concerns.
President Trump defended Hegseth on social media after he spoke.
The House is expected to vote on the impeachment effort in the coming days.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Washington.
>> Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer is demanding answers
following President Trump's defense of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Hao Huang.
>> The press reports that Trump was briefed more than a year ago,
that NVIDIA's CEO was having an affair with his suspected Chinese spy,
and Trump didn't do anything, anything about it.
Can you believe that?
>> NVIDIA is a major producer of computer chips.
Senator Schumer says Congress must quickly approve new restrictions
on chip exports to China as a matter of national security.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio says talks today aimed at ending
Russia's war against Ukraine were very productive.
Secretary Rubio also says the goal is to expand those talks to include Europe.
>> What's really important is that the Europeans are at the table.
They'll be discussing with our people.
They've been working very closely with Jared and Steve,
who are there on every step along the way.
And it's actually our goal at some point to expand this trilateral.
So it's not just the US, Ukraine, and Russia,
but also that the Europeans be represented at that table directly.
>> The first day of talks in Abu Dhabi lasted about four hours.
This was the first meeting since February.
Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022.
A new report from the New York Federal Reserve finds credit card debt
increased across the US households over the summer.
But NPR's Stephen Bizaha says households are doing better,
keeping up with the payments.
>> Households added another $52 billion in credit card debt by September
compared to a year earlier.
That brings the total debt to just under $1.3 trillion.
New York Fed researchers found a slight drop in how much of that debt
is considered seriously delinquent.
They also reported a sharp rise in consumers borrowing against houses.
Home equity loan balances grew by about $23 billion July through September,
the largest increase since 2005.
Fed researchers say that's likely driven by homeowners
having a lot of equity built up in their homes
and using that to borrow money at cheaper rates.
>> You're listening to NPR.
Washington State produces millions of pounds of pumpkins every year.
But after Halloween, what happens to all those pumpkins
that don't get picked from the patch?
>> Northwest Public Broadcasting's Lauren Gallup flotted out
to some farms to find out.
>> When Double R Farms closes its pumpkin patch for the year,
the leftovers don't go to waste.
Instead, the fowl and fauna --
>> They have a feast right now.
>> As Jerry Ruiz walks down a gravel path from her house to the fields,
flocks fly overhead and land in the fields of mowed down pumpkins
and the old corn maze.
>> All the geese are loving it right now.
And they're going to -- they've already been over to the pumpkins
and the crows also, crows and the Canadian geese.
>> Ruiz says after a few weeks, the birds are done with the crop.
The rest decomposes and goes back into the soil,
adding nutrients for next year's harvest.
For NPR News, I'm Lauren Gallup in Puyallup, Washington.
>> The co-founder of Airbnb is donating $100 million
to the San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department.
Brian Chesky's donation is the largest private contribution
to the city by just one person.
The Recreation and Parks Department has proposed a budget of $271 million,
making Chesky's donation more than a third
of the department's annual spending.
The department previously projected a shortfall of $15 million,
but is well on its way to eliminating that shortfall.
On Wall Street, just after closing, the Dow was down 144 points.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth defends himself at rare press conference amid House impeachment effort
Senator Chuck Schumer demands answers after Trump defends NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang amid spy affair reports
Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Ukraine-Russia peace talks in Abu Dhabi were productive, aims to add Europe
New York Fed reports credit card debt rose by $52 billion, while home equity borrowing hit record increase
Washington State pumpkin patch leftovers feed geese and crows before decomposing into farm soil
Airbnb co-founder Brian Chesky donates $100 million to San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department
Dow falls 144 points at the close of trading on Wall Street
